schema_note: Field-typed. Machine-readable values carry a _token suffix and contain NO whitespace. Prose lives ONLY in the declared allow-list below and is never parsed by any reader. The allow-list is a declared SET, not a name-suffix test (s3.7): a bundle spelled its prose field bare 'note' and a '.endswith("_note")' guard returned False and parsed it.
prose_field_allow_list_note: A reader consumes ONLY the fields it was told to consume (s3.7, allow-list direction). Any field NOT in this list is machine-readable. Bundle-side prose fields that no reader may touch are enumerated separately under bundle_prose_fields.

child_key_components.why_note: THIS BUNDLE HAS NO 'kind' FIELD on child-key components. The sub-keys actually present are name / value / resolved_on_view, plus a bare 'note' on 48 of 296 entries. A reader written against a 'kind'-bearing map matches nothing here, returns None, and the build reports a false SOURCE gap (s2). Generators MUST read name/value/resolved_on_view from this profile.
child_key_components.sibling_fields_note: child_key (leg name, 435) and child_key_value (rendered value, 524) sit beside child_key_components (160) and must all be read. See map_fields.CORRECTION_field_names.child_key_spellings.

CORRECTION_field_names.claim_corrected_note: A standing instruction stated 'the child-key field is key_name; there is NO child_key_value field in this map - I probed for one and got a confident zero.' BOTH HALVES ARE WRONG and the zero was a reader defect (s1.1, s2). MEASURED on the SETTLED file:
CORRECTION_field_names.why_this_matters_note: key_name holds the HUB's business-key NAME, not a child key - 37 distinct values like 'Policy Number (canonical contract key)'. It is DISJOINT from child_key_value: ZERO rows populate both. A generator told that key_name is the child-key field would write a hub key NAME into a child key, and those values are PROSE CARRYING PARENTHESES, so 'Policy Number (canonical contract key)' would reach generated SQL as a child-key column - precisely the s3 defect that produced MODEL_SINGLE_ACTIVE_BUILD_SIDE_MULTI_ACTIVE_ASK. Note also that the coordinator's own pinned R6_childkey_value_kind.json is BUILT from child_key_value, so the claim that the field does not exist contradicts the artefact supplied alongside it. Generators MUST read child_key_value and child_key_components; key_name is a HUB-key field and belongs nowhere near a child key.
CORRECTION_field_names.disjointness_note: ASSERTED, not assumed: over all 7354 container dicts, 830 populate EITHER key_name or child_key_value and 0 populate BOTH. The two spellings are DISJOINT, so a reader must read BOTH in BOTH containers - reading one yields a uniform absence indistinguishable from 'this run has no child keys'. Same shape as OPUS Health's key_name-on-target versus child_key-on-augmentation split.
CORRECTION_field_names.three_state_note: ABSENT, PRESENT_NULL and the literal string 'None' are THREE states, not two. On the 54 MEMBER group rows key_name and instance are PRESENT-AND-NULL while child_key_value and child_key_components are ABSENT ENTIRELY. Both mean 'no discriminator' so refuse-and-declare is unchanged, but the declared artefact records WHICH state it found per row, because a future reader fixing 'null' would not look for 'absent'. Carried in build_artifacts/reports/declared_unresolved_grain.json.
CORRECTION_field_names.child_key_spellings_note: THE FULL PICTURE, and it is richer than either census that preceded it. There are THREE child-key fields and they are COMPLEMENTARY, not alternatives: child_key holds the LEG NAME ('Certificate Number', 'Active Sequence Number'); child_key_value holds the RENDERED VALUE ('Per-Member Certificate', 'Benefit Head Code = DEATH'); child_key_components holds the STRUCTURED legs as name/value/resolved_on_view. They co-occur: 139 containers populate all three, 248 populate child_key+child_key_value, 116 child_key_value alone and 48 child_key ALONE - a leg name with no value. A reader must read ALL THREE in BOTH containers. key_name is the fourth and is NOT a child key at all: it holds the HUB business-key name, appears only on target, and NEVER co-occurs with any child-key field (all 306 are key_name-alone), which is independent confirmation that it is a different concept.

bundle_prose_fields.why_note: Each was tested BY VALUE, not by name. target.transformation holds 'code->decode'; key_derivation holds 'childkey[column_as_instance]: child key Member Reference = {MEMBER_ID} | Condition Code = <TYPE>, BOTH declared legs resolved...'. Note the BARE spelling 'note' (not '_note') on target, augmentation, reanchor and inside components: a '.endswith("_note")' guard returns False on it and parses it. s3.7 realised in THIS bundle, so the exclusion is this declared set.

component_kinds_note: STEP 2's census is legitimately empty here and the zero is EXPLAINED rather than trusted: the field does not exist. 324 component entries (28 target + 296 augmentation) were enumerated and their sub-keys censused instead.
grammar_note: MERGED population: the 115 contract (833) plus delta 3 (501). Delta 3 introduces NO new grammar form and leaves 0 expressions unclassified -- it uses the same five forms this reader already knew. Per form: LNK_composite 37+2, coalesce_lead 4+0, md5_normalise_upper 31+42, nullif_concat_namespaced 153+81, nullif_trim_bare 608+376.
parse_residue_note: Residue swept over resolved_key.expression: 37 strings retain 'LNK(' and all 37 are accounted for by the LNK_composite form; UNACCOUNTED = 0. spine[ and >> survivors = 0. Separately, 127 strings contain '->' and 612 contain brace tokens, but ALL of those live in prose fields (transformation, key_derivation) or in resolvable operand templates, never in a key expression.
hierarchy_walk_note: STEP 3's edge-field hunt was NOT run, because the grammar census found zero walk operators and therefore no destination to resolve. Stated rather than silently skipped: no parent/child edge field was sought, no edge count was computed, and NO ancestry or lowest-common-ancestor claim is made anywhere in this profile. 00_tables_index.json is not part of this bundle.

canonical_key.decision_note: Adopts v2's EXPLICIT hash, visible in the emitted SQL, plus legacy's NAMESPACE. The namespace is a MEASURED collision guard, not decoration: v2 emits md5(upper(HUB_ASSESSMENT_BK__SCRUTINY_NO)) and md5(upper(HUB_PROPOSAL_BK__SCRUTINY_NO)) from the SAME column SCRUTINY_NO, so without a namespace those two hubs would share key values for the same input. Legacy already namespaces 1822 of 1822 hash-key declarations, zero exceptions. Setting the one-line switch to false reverts to v2's literal form md5(upper(<bk>)).
canonical_key.feasibility_note: Not an argument but a running artifact: opus_health_v2_dv_dbt already emits 364 explicit md5( calls across 181 of its 329 models and invokes only dbt built-ins (ref 575, config 329, source 32) with ZERO package macros. So 'compute every hash key explicitly in SQL, no macro hashing' is already implemented at scale on one of the two halves. No reason was found that this cannot work.
canonical_key.risk_note: CRITICAL PRECISION: the namespace separates one hub's key space from another's. It does NOTHING for two registries INSIDE one hub. hub_policy's own caveat registers POLICY_REF vs POLICY_NO as UNDETERMINED, and 'HUB_POLICY|' prefixes both identically. Nobody may read the namespace decision as resolving reconciliation.

legacy_key_forms.legacy_hash_algorithm_note: 0 md5( / sha2( / hash( calls in all 1330 .sql. Every hash is inside automate_dv macros (stage 960, sat 83, link 58, ma_sat 41, hub 20; 1162 invocations total), and automate_dv is DECLARED in packages.yml (>=0.11.0,<0.12.0) but NOT INSTALLED: dbt_packages/ and package-lock.yml are both absent. The only algorithm statement in legacy's docs names dbt_utils.generate_surrogate_key, and legacy's own README says that is explicitly NOT the active build's formula ('different hashing formula'). The live algorithm is therefore an INFERENCE from the package default, never a documented fact.
legacy_key_forms.packages_yml_note: Correction to the brief: v2 has NO packages.yml at all, which is stronger than an empty one - it declares no dependency rather than declaring none.

hk_vs_hkey.detail_note: The caller flagged that a legacy augmented stage hashes into PARTY_HK while hub_party declares src_pk 'PARTY_HKEY', and asked for measurement rather than a verdict. MEASURED: the split is HUB/LINK-FEED vs SATELLITE-FEED, NOT standard vs augmented. PARTY_HK has 59 STANDARD producers (all stg2_sat_*) and only 10 augmented (stg2_aug_*); PARTY_HKEY's 199 producers are all stg2_link_ / stg2_hub_ / stg2_<entity>_ / stg2_addrusage_ / stg2_shared_. No model produces both spellings. The same pattern holds for POLICY, CLAIM and RISK_OBJECT. Both spellings render 'HUB_PARTY|' || <col>, so they AGREE IN VALUE and differ only in name and in which track emits them. And all 267 hub source_model entries across all 20 legacy hubs produce their declared src_pk: ZERO gaps. NOT BROKEN - the caller was right not to call it so on a name mismatch.

per_hub_bk_note: unit: legacy = distinct namespaced-NK right-hand expressions, and the distinct lowercase identifiers inside them, over 1822 legacy hashed_columns declarations parsed from emitted SQL; v2 = distinct HUB_X_BK__<COL> suffixes in vault/hubs and vault/links. The caller's five spot figures all reproduce EXACTLY: CLAIM 12 expressions vs 6 BK columns, ASSESSMENT 9 vs 1 (SCRUTINY_NO), DISTRIBUTION_CHANNEL 10 vs 3, COVERAGE 5 vs 1 (CVR_CODE), CASE 6 vs 1 (CASHLESS_IN_ID). CAUTION: v2's two shared LINKS show 0 BK columns under this matcher, which is a READER ARTIFACT, not absence - v2 keys its links by hub HK legs (HUB_PARTY_HK), not by LNK_X_BK__ columns.

registry_reconciliation.risk_note: Unifying the hash form does NOT produce a joinable hub; it produces ONE key space holding TWO sets of registries. 6 of the 14 shared hubs have ZERO BK-column overlap between the runs, so the problem is WORSE than hub_party alone and worse than reported upstream. Whether CUST_ID, PARTNER_ID, IMD_CODE, HOS_ID and RM_CODE denote the same parties is a question about the DATA, answerable from neither the map nor the SQL. v2 keys HUB_PROPOSAL and HUB_ASSESSMENT from the same SCRUTINY_NO column, which the namespace now separates.

v2_header_count_discrepancy.why_note: v2's hub_party header states '13 identifier populations' while 15 distinct HUB_PARTY_BK__ columns over 17 feed slots are actually emitted. RAISED, not resolved and not edited: the v2 build owns its own count (s5.7, s9.9).

carried_forward_caveats.carried_forward_verbatim_note: FIVE s9.8 reconciliation blocks exist across the two originals, not one. The coordinator named hub_party; hub_claim, hub_policy, hub_product and lnk_party_role carry their own and are equally unrecoverable after load. ALL FIVE must be reproduced VERBATIM in the consolidated model headers. lnk_party_role's is the most consequential: it records that the one-leg link hash key is BYTE-EQUAL to HUB_PARTY_HK and that the role token is absent from the link key entirely. Losing any one of these in the merge is the single real regression available in this assignment.

sibling.convention_note: COUNTED from both siblings' emitted satellite SQL (124 and 87 satellite models), never read from any description including this one. Both siblings agree on UPPER_SNAKE, so this convention is uncontested and is inherited rather than established.
sibling.hashdiff_note: s7.7's exact configuration, measured: legacy writes a BARE HASHDIFF on all 124 standard AND its 15 augmented satellites, while v2 writes <SAT_NAME>_HASHDIFF on both of its tracks. A project-wide answer inherited from 'the sibling' is wrong in one direction, because THERE ARE TWO SIBLINGS AND THEY CONFLICT - s7.1/s7.2 do not decide this and neither does the model, since a hashdiff column name is a convention and not a model property. Recommending v2's explicit form for consistency with the explicit-key decision, but NOT RATIFIED: the caller has not ruled. This interacts with the estate's open shared-vault hashdiff problem, because 62 shared tables become ONE loader and therefore ONE hashdiff chain over the UNION of both feeds.

shared_vault_tables.unit_note: unit = exact .sql basename located in a vault directory
shared_vault_tables.matcher_note: models/**/*.sql basenames. Vault dirs: health_dv_dbt automate_dv/standard/{hubs,links,satellites} plus automate_dv/augmented/satellites; opus_health_v2_dv_dbt vault/{hubs,links,satellites} plus augmented/. Reference models are NOT shared and are excluded (legacy ref_exclusion, v2 ref_bank_branch_ifsc). The same 62 results from an all-basename match across every .sql, so no staging or reject_log name collides with a vault name.
shared_vault_tables.two_62s_note: 62 shared vault TABLES and 62 cross-run (satellite, attribute) PAIRS are DIFFERENT UNITS that coincide on a number, and they are not reconciled anywhere in this profile. A THIRD near-miss is also kept apart: the map reports 48 shared satellites plus 15 shared anchors = 63 map-side names, which is neither of the 62s.

r8_source_precedence.precedence_fires_note: 62 of 62 - TRUE BY CONSTRUCTION of the input set, which is DEFINED as the pairs having writers in BOTH runs, so legacy-only and v2-only are both 0 by definition. This is NOT an independent measurement and must not be read as one. The informative figures are 607 columns over 19 satellites.
r8_source_precedence.mechanism_note: One row per hub key, one hashdiff over the UNION, and where both runs write one attribute a DECLARED precedence decides, named per attribute in the satellite header (s9.8), with all 607 columns enumerated in the artefact. Null-padding does not solve two writers of the SAME attribute, and adding RECORD_SOURCE to the key would silently change the satellite's grain - forbidden.

r6_r7_childkeys.remedy_note: ZERO of 422 legacy blocks name a leg - not one - so there is no spelling to normalise, because there is no leg naming to normalise from. The original 'normalise legacy's labels to v2's codes' instruction was withdrawn and must not be implemented. For any shared multi-active satellite whose legacy feed has no resolvable child key: emit the feed with NO fabricated discriminator and DECLARE the unresolved grain, in the satellite header (s9.8) AND in a countable artefact. A declared unresolved grain is recoverable; an invented one is not. This mirrors the travel build's src_cdk:0, which refused an unresolvable key and landed the source faithfully (s9.8). Never invent a child key (s7.4).

SAT_COMMON_CONTACT.model_childkey: Contact Point Type + Contact Priority Order

r6_r7_childkeys.per_satellite_note: unit = block, i.e. a (row, container) pair carrying this satellite as its home across target/best_home_satellite/new_satellite. 'naming a leg' = at least one child_key_components entry with a name, or a child_key_value containing '='.

relabel_exception.resolution_note: INDEPENDENTLY DERIVED and it refutes both upstream figures: 30 blocks, ALL bucket E_PROSE, ZERO bare-code, 15 distinct values x 2 feeds = 30 exact. The mapper's 26 and the coordinator's '26 prose + 4 bare' hypothesis are both wrong - this satellite has no bare-code blocks at all; the only 6 bucket-B blocks in the entire bundle sit on SAT_RISK_HEALTH_MEMBER_MEDICAL. Relabel all 30 concept-for-concept, and ONLY where v2 actually has a counterpart code; refuse and declare any value with no counterpart rather than coining a code.

condition_satellite_three_defects.defect_1_note: The 'Member Reference' leg is ABSENT on all 11 blocks, so every member with a given condition collides onto ONE row. This is the sharpest case in the set and must be named verbatim in the satellite header.
condition_satellite_three_defects.defect_2_note: The 'Condition Code' leg is spelled TWO WAYS, one per SOURCE TABLE, so one condition becomes two child rows. The mechanism is cross-FEED vocabulary divergence INSIDE one run, not a run disagreeing with itself: BA_HCP_PROD_8439_CLH_LOADER (MD_* columns, prose) yields 'Diabetes' from MD_DIABETES, while BJAZ_HCF_MEMBER_DTLS (*_LOAD columns, bare) yields 'DIABETES' from DIABETES_LOAD. Measured case-insensitive collisions within the satellite: diabetes, hypertension, obesity.
condition_satellite_three_defects.defect_3_note: 'Cholesterol Disorders' (MD_CHOLESTEROL_DISORDERS) versus 'HYPERLIPIDEMIA' (HYPERLIPIDEMIA_LOAD) is a SYNONYM CANDIDATE, NOT an assertion - plausibly one condition under a clinical and a lay name. It needs a clinician or the source owner. NOT normalised and NOT asserted.
condition_satellite_three_defects.asymmetry_note: The two vocabularies are NOT two spellings of one list: they overlap on 3 conditions and diverge on 3 more. prose-only (no bare counterpart) = 'Cholesterol Disorders', 'Heart Disease'; bare-only (no prose counterpart) = 'BMI', 'HYPERLIPIDEMIA', 'OTHER'. A case-folding normaliser would merge the three overlapping conditions and SILENTLY LEAVE THE REST SPLIT.

r6_r7_childkeys.r7_note: Compound child keys that legacy resolves on zero or one leg: SAT_COMMON_CONTACT (Contact Point Type + Contact Priority Order), SAT_RISK_HEALTH_MEMBER_MEDICAL (Member Reference + Condition Code), SAT_POLICY_COVERAGE_SCHEDULE (Coverage Reference + Coverage Sequence) and SAT_LNK_PARTY_ROLE_CORE (Role Code + Role Sequence). Build both legs where they resolve; refuse and declare where they do not. Recorded as the FIFTH instance of this class on the estate. IMPORTANT COUNTER-FINDING: v2 ALSO under-keys - it resolves both declared legs on only 5 of 15 SAT_COMMON_CONTACT blocks, and 1 of 2 legs on its single SAT_LNK_PARTY_ROLE_CORE block - so 'legacy under-keys, v2 is conformant' is NOT universal and s7.8's model-decides rule applies to both sides.

sat_common_contact_populations.population_note: 89 = 81 + 8, reconciled. State which population is meant every time: the 89 and the 81 were conflated upstream and they answer different questions.

additional_refuse_and_declare.shared_correction_note: Called a '16th SHARED multi-active satellite' upstream. MEASURED: all 59 rows are opus_health_legacy_v4 and ZERO are opus_health_v2, and sat_risk_person_member is in the 140 LEGACY-ONLY vault tables, NOT in the 62 shared. So it is a 17th refuse-and-declare satellite but it is NOT shared, and the shared multi-active count stays at 16. It needs a single-feed loader, not a dual-feed one.
additional_refuse_and_declare.source_table_correction_note: The 54-row GROUP is single-table (BJAZ_WS_FAMILY_DTLS_BANDHAN), but the 59-row SATELLITE draws on 5 source tables. State which population is meant.
additional_refuse_and_declare.population_trap_note: BUILD FROM THE GROUP (54), NOT FROM THE RE-ANCHOR LIST (45). The 9 'Pre-Existing Disease Description' rows sit in the same repeating group with the same null child key but were never touched by the re-anchor pass. A build taking its refuse-and-declare population from the re-anchored rows would leave those 9 SILENTLY UNDECLARED. Declare all 54, and record the 59-row satellite total too since the other 5 rows share the null child key.
additional_refuse_and_declare.do_not_synthesise_note: Do NOT synthesise 'Member Sequence' from the column name. The ordinal looks trivially derivable from MEMBER1..8, and that is exactly the fabricated-discriminator trap: the SELF slot carries NO NUMBER AT ALL, so any derivation must INVENT a value for it. Inventing the discriminator is what the travel build's src_cdk:0 exists to prevent. Routed to the mapper's Stage 6.
additional_refuse_and_declare.collapse_instrument_note: check_collapse SKIPS this satellite, so its reported violations exclude it and its silence here is NOT a clean bill.

collapse_measurement.detail_note: Stage 6 never ran on the legacy half, and check_collapse DELIBERATELY SKIPS a multi-active target whose child key is unresolved. So every legacy collapse count - including the 16 single-active fan-in violations (43 columns), the 29 augmentation fan-in groups (150 columns) and the 8 dangling redundant_of - is a LOWER BOUND. The 286 bucket-A blocks are UNJUDGED, not clean. A check that skips its hardest cases returns a number about the easy ones (s1.16 with s1.30). No zero from that instrument may be reported as clean.

collapse_traps_note: No discriminator-shaped-but-identical column was identified, and the empty list is EXPLAINED rather than offered as a clean bill: the failure mode in THIS bundle is the OPPOSITE shape. Child-key legs are ABSENT (422 legacy blocks name no leg) rather than present-and-non-discriminating. The four compound-key satellites under r6_r7_childkeys.r7_note are the equivalent hazard here, and the spec builder must assert that no FABRICATED leg appears in any key or child key.
renumbering_ordinals_note: Declared child-key leg names that are per-parent sequences: each changes when a sibling row is added or removed, so none is hub-grade (s5.1). They ARE declared legs in data_7.js, so they are not excluded - they are FLAGGED: a leg built on one of these inherits the instability, and s5.2 requires checking every spelling. 'Active Sequence Number' (SAT_PARTY_DIGITAL_IDENTITY) is the same concept under a fourth name, which is exactly the two-spellings defect s5.2 records.
layers_note: NO walk-only casts and NO ancestor resolvers: the grammar census found zero walk operators, so s6's walk-only and resolver layers have nothing to range over in this LOB. The layer set follows v2's shape, which is the dependency-free sibling and the one whose structure the explicit-key decision adopts.

bespoke_layers.name: dual_feed_satellite_loader
bespoke_layers.reason_note: One loader per shared vault table with BOTH feeds as SEPARATE sources, reconciled by a DECLARED SOURCE PRECEDENCE over the 607 R8 columns. No standard s6 layer expresses two INDEPENDENT writers of the SAME attribute on one satellite row: the standard satellite layer unions feeders that are disjoint by construction, which is exactly the assumption the union breaks. Declared exception under s6.5, scoped to the 62 shared tables.

bespoke_layers.name: declared_unresolved_grain_register
bespoke_layers.reason_note: A countable artefact enumerating every satellite whose child key is REFUSED rather than fabricated, mirrored into each affected satellite header (s9.8). Not a model layer but a required build output; declared here so it is never an unannounced extra generator.

layer_plan_one_loader.mechanism_note: For each of the 62 shared tables: ONE model, with the two feeds kept as SEPARATE sources tagged by RECORD_SOURCE, one hash key in the canonical form, one hashdiff over the UNION of both feeds' attributes null-padded to the satellite, and the R8 precedence applied per attribute. The 140 legacy-only and 45 v2-only tables get a single-feed loader each. 62 + 140 + 45 = 247 vault tables.

build_directives.directive_note: Canonical hub key md5(upper('HUB_X|' || <bk>)), emitted explicitly; no macro computes a hash.
build_directives.mechanism: names module renders the hash inline; a macro may assemble hub/sat/link mechanics only with src_pk pointing at a PRE-COMPUTED column.

build_directives.directive_note: Declared source precedence per attribute over 607 columns; never a key change, never RECORD_SOURCE in the key.
build_directives.mechanism: precedence artefact plus a per-attribute coalesce in declared order; the precedence is NAMED in the satellite header.

build_directives.directive_note: Refuse and declare unresolved child-key grain. Relabel ONLY SAT_POLICY_DISCOUNT_LOADING_APPLIED's 30 blocks, concept-for-concept, and only where v2 has a counterpart code.
build_directives.mechanism: child-key renderer emits no leg it cannot resolve; every refusal is written into the satellite header AND the unresolved-grain register.

build_directives.directive_note: Build every declared child-key leg that resolves on the 4 compound-key shared satellites; refuse the rest.

self_assertion.assert_note: A *_token value containing whitespace is a HARD FAILURE and names its key. Every other space-bearing string value is REPORTED for review, never failed. The first draft of this gate failed any non-_note key whose value held a space, which would have fired on the legitimate key template and on every genuine attribute name like 'Classification Effective Date'. A space is not the property; BEING READ AS A TOKEN is. A gate that fails on benign data gets switched off and then protects nothing (s1.12).

matcher_discipline.rule_note: REPRODUCED on the settled file: r'\bMEMBER[1-8]\b' matches 0 of the 54 group rows while the substring r'MEMBER[1-8]' matches 48 (plus 6 SELF = 54). The columns are MEMBER1DOB, MEMBER1GENDER, MEMBER1NAME - an alphanumeric follows the digit, so the word boundary never occurs. Identical mechanism to spine_present defeating r'\bspine\b'. EVERY column-name sweep in this build uses a substring or explicit character class, and states its matcher beside its count.

instance_labels.rule_note: P_ and M_ mean PERMANENT and MAILING, not proposer/member. The prefix reads naturally as proposer/member and that reading is WRONG. GOOD NEWS, measured: the settled map ALREADY carries the right answer in target.instance - P_CITY instance='permanent', M_CITY instance='mailing', 10 of 13 rows resolved on SAT_COMMON_ADDRESS. So the build must READ target.instance and never infer an instance from a column prefix. The remaining 3 rows (P_EMAIL, M_EMAIL, M_MOBILE on SAT_COMMON_CONTACT) carry instance=None and are distinguished by ATTRIBUTE instead (Email Address vs Alternate Email Address), which needs no instance split. Inferring proposer/member here would have overwritten a member's mailing address with their permanent one.

remaining_fan_ins.detail_note: 11 single-active fan-ins remain, pre-existing and untouched by the Stage 6.5 pass. The sharpest puts 7 columns on one attribute. These need instance splits and none has a resolved key, so the disposition is the same: refuse and declare. Plus 8 dangling redundant_of pointers.
